休: 亻 + 木 gives a useful person-and-tree connection. The traveler, clothing and 3D depth are invented teaching choices.
木: Use the tree shape to remember 木. Its meanings include both tree and wood; the table is a memory scene.
人: The two strokes provide a visual anchor for a person. This character view can be reused wherever 人 appears.
林: Two 木 components make a compact visual cue for woods. Learn the complete character 林 alongside the scene.
森: Three 木 components offer a memorable cue for dense woods. Compare its arrangement with 林.
清: 氵 contributes the water association; 青 is the phonetic component. The lesson uses the clear sense, not the Qing dynasty name.
晴: 日 connects to the sun and weather; 青 is the phonetic component. Compare qíng with qīng: the tone differs.
请: 讠 relates to speech; 青 supplies a pronunciation clue. The invitation belongs to this word's use, not to a literal green object.
情: 忄 relates to the heart and feelings; 青 is the phonetic component. Compare this with 清, 晴 and 请.
青: This lesson selects the blue-green color sense. The word can have other senses; do not carry this color meaning into every phonetic compound.
河: 氵 relates to water and 可 is the historical phonetic component. Modern hé and kě are not identical pronunciations.
可: This lesson selects permission or possibility. Its standalone meaning does not explain its phonetic role inside 河.
月: The moon is a useful cue here. A similar-looking component can represent 肉 in body-related characters; shape alone does not decide origin.
肝: The left component derives from 肉 (flesh), despite resembling 月; 干 is phonetic. Use the organ scene, not a moon story.
手: The hand is a useful standalone meaning. Related words can use 手 for a person, skill or an idiomatic relationship.
手掌: 手 anchors the hand; 掌 identifies its palm. The close-up scene teaches the whole word's specific body part.
手机: 手 suggests hand and 机 machine. A machine held in your hand is a mnemonic; 手机 conventionally means mobile phone.
高手: 手 here refers to a skilled person. 高手 means expert; it does not describe a physically high hand.
分手: Separating hands is a mnemonic for parting. The word can describe a breakup or parting company; the scene selects a relationship context.
对手: 手 refers to a person in this word: an opponent. Facing players express the relationship more accurately than two isolated hands.
快乐: 乐 is lè here. Store the pronunciation with 快乐; compare 音乐, where the same written character is yuè.
音乐: 音 and 乐 connect to sound and music; 乐 is yuè here. The character's geometry stays the same as in 快乐.
银行: 银 relates to silver or money; 行 here is háng, a business or establishment. 银行 means a financial bank.
行走: 行 and 走 both connect to going or walking. 行 is xíng here, unlike háng in 银行.
长大: 长 is zhǎng, grow, followed by 大, big. Together they describe growing up.
长江: 长 is cháng, long; 江 is river. The complete proper name identifies the Yangtze, not just any long river.
重要: 重 is zhòng here. Importance is the target sense; a heavy object would only be an optional memory metaphor.
重复: 重 is chóng, again. The scene repeats a phrase, making the action and reading clear.
便宜: The inexpensive sense is pián yi, with neutral-tone yi. The dictionary also records biàn yí for a different sense.
方便: 便 is biàn here. Learn the convenient situation as a whole rather than importing pián from 便宜.
东西: For things or stuff, pronounce dōng xi with neutral-tone xi. Dōng xī means east and west; those directions do not explain this lesson's sense.
马虎: 马虎 means careless. A horse-and-tiger picture could be a shape mnemonic, but it would not establish the word's origin or usage.
咖啡: This is a borrowing. The coffee scene anchors its meaning; the characters mainly help represent its sound.
葡萄: Learn 葡萄 together as grape. Splitting it into unrelated standalone character meanings does not explain the fruit.
蝴蝶: Learn 蝴蝶 as a whole word. The 虫 component offers a broad creature association, not a complete explanation of butterfly.
巧克力: This is a borrowing for chocolate. Avoid deriving the food from the standalone meanings of 巧, 克 and 力.
不好意思: The situation selects the apologetic or embarrassed use. Tone and context matter; the phrase is more than four independent glosses.
莫名其妙: Teach the baffling situation first. The short scene demonstrates a use of the expression; it is not an origin story.
理所当然: Returning something borrowed illustrates what is expected as a matter of course. This is a usage scene, not a historical account.
自相矛盾: The contradictory box claims demonstrate the meaning. 矛 and 盾 are spear and shield, but this scene is not a retelling of the historical anecdote.
画蛇添足: The literal drawing supplies a strong cue: adding feet to a snake. The figurative meaning is spoiling something through an unnecessary addition.
一举两得: One action produces two benefits. Count the single journey and its two outcomes in the memory scene.
不知不觉: The repeated 不 frames the absence of knowing and noticing. The reading scene illustrates time passing unnoticed.
电脑: 电, electricity, plus 脑, brain, provides a useful electric-brain mnemonic. The ordinary word means computer.
飞机: 飞, fly, plus 机, machine, gives a useful flying-machine connection for airplane.
火车站: 火车 is train and 站 is station. Group the word as 火车 + 站 rather than three separate objects.
图书馆: 图书 means books and 馆 a building or establishment. Group the word as 图书 + 馆.
洗手间: 洗手 means wash hands and 间 means room. The whole word is a conventional name for a washroom.
自行车: Treat 自行车 as bicycle. The riding scene supports the complete word; literal character glosses alone do not uniquely identify a bicycle.
公共汽车: 公共, public, modifies 汽车, motor vehicle. The conventional meaning is bus.
打电话: Group 打 + 电话: the verb collocates with telephone to mean make a call. Do not portray hitting a phone.
打篮球: 打 is the verb used with 篮球 for playing basketball. Its hitting sense should not be substituted mechanically.
眼镜: 眼 relates to eyes and 镜 to optical glass or mirrors. Eyeglasses provide the whole-word target; compare 眼睛, eyes.
眼睛: This word means eyes. Compare jing here with jìng in 眼镜; similar sounds and shapes name different things.
有名: 有, have, and 名, name or reputation, give a useful connection to being well-known.
月亮: 月 supplies the moon connection. Learn yuè liang as the whole noun; the second syllable is neutral in the selected reading.
冰箱: 冰, ice, and 箱, box, offer an ice-box mnemonic. The modern everyday referent is refrigerator.
地铁: 地 relates to ground and 铁 to iron. The conventional word is subway; its meaning is not simply any underground iron.
地球: 地 connects to earth and 球 to a sphere. The whole word identifies planet Earth.
牛奶: 牛, cow, specifies the source of 奶, milk.
羊肉: 羊 identifies sheep or goats and 肉 means meat. The word can refer to mutton, lamb or goat meat according to context.
鸡蛋: 鸡, chicken, specifies the source of 蛋, egg.
果汁: 果, fruit, plus 汁, juice, directly supports the fruit-juice scene.
手表: 手 connects to the hand or wrist area; 表 means watch here. Reuse the character shape from 手机 but teach this distinct object.
上班: This means go to work or be on duty. A workplace scene is clearer than treating 上 only as upward movement.
马上: This lesson selects immediately. A horse with something above it would be an arbitrary shape mnemonic, not an explanation of this usage.
小心: 小心 means be careful. A physically small heart is not the meaning; the careful carrying scene supplies context.
关心: 关心 means care about. Do not force 关's shut sense into an account of this compound.
放心: The message of safe arrival explains feeling reassured. A heart object could be a memory prop, but is not required for the word meaning.
伤心: 伤, hurt, and 心, heart, provide an emotional rather than anatomical connection: deeply sad.
好吃: 好 is hǎo here and 吃 is eat. The combination describes food that is good to eat: delicious.
爱好: 好 is hào here. A hobby is something you enjoy; compare hǎo in 好吃.
故事: The narrative sense is gù shi, with neutral-tone shi. The source has another reading for old practice.
妻子: The wife sense is qī zi, with neutral-tone zi. Do not select the separate qī zǐ reading for wife and children.
头发: 头 is head and 发 is fà in isolation for hair. In this word the source records tóu fa, with a neutral second syllable.
花园: 花, flower, and 园, garden, create a direct visual connection to a garden.
黑板: 黑, black, modifies 板, board. The classroom board is the whole-word object.
面条: 面 refers to flour or dough here and 条 to strips. Long dough strips provide a useful noodle connection.
好处: For benefit, select hǎo chu. The other source reading hǎo chǔ describes being easy to get along with.
重点: 重 is zhòng here, indicating importance, followed by 点, point. Compare 重复, where 重 is chóng.
知识: Learn zhī shi as knowledge. A word-level reading prevents mechanically assigning a full tone to every character.
小说: 小说 is a novel or fiction. The small-speech glosses of 小 and 说 do not adequately explain this meaning.
熊猫: The complete word names a panda. Bear and cat can be playful memory cues, but do not imply that a panda is a hybrid animal.
新闻: 新, new, and 闻, hear or news, give a useful new-information connection.
